frontmatter.name: code-explain
frontmatter.description: Explain code the user pasted or described. Use when they ask what a snippet does, why it fails, or how control flow moves. Do not use it to invent a large new program.

frontmatter.name: cursor-phraser
frontmatter.description: Turn a request to add, fix, or build something in a codebase into one brief for a Cursor cloud agent. Use when the user wants a handoff they can paste into Cursor or a Background Agent, not an edit made inside Meridian.

frontmatter.name: daily-planning
frontmatter.description: Build a realistic plan for today or a short block of work. Use when the user wants priorities, a schedule, or help deciding what to do next.

frontmatter.name: image
frontmatter.description: Generate an image with /image. Use when the user asks to create, draw, or generate a picture from a description; calls image_generate and stores a backend record.

frontmatter.name: itinerary-day
frontmatter.description: Turn a trip brief or the pinned map into a day-by-day schedule. Use when the user wants the days ordered, not a new destination.

frontmatter.name: packing-list
frontmatter.description: Build a packing list from the trip type, dates, and destination weather. Use when the user asks what to pack or bring.

frontmatter.name: prompt-refine
frontmatter.description: Rewrite a prompt so a local model can follow it. Use when the user pastes a prompt, system message, or instruction and wants it sharper, shorter, or more reliable.

frontmatter.name: travel-research
frontmatter.description: Outline what to look up for a trip: fares, weather, getting around, and entry rules. Use when the user wants comparisons or sources, not a finished booking.

frontmatter.name: trip-planning
frontmatter.description: Plan a trip: destination, dates, constraints, budget frame, and an itinerary outline. Use when the user wants to shape a journey before booking anything.

frontmatter.name: web-research
frontmatter.description: Plan and carry out a short web research brief. Use when the user asks to look something up, compare claims, or understand a topic from pages on the internet.
